env.#1: URL of THIS application's MCP endpoint, e.g. https://testshop.suissetec.ch/mcp - byte for byte what the hub puts in "aud".
env.#2: Key set of the hub (the issuing authorization server), used to verify the token signature.
env.#3: Base URL of the hub, compared verbatim with the "iss" claim - no trailing slash.
env.#5: Optional. Only set this when resource_metadata_url is enabled in packages/suissetec_mcp_auth.yaml:

post-install-output: * Set <info>SUISSETEC_MCP_AUDIENCE</info> (this application's /mcp URL), <info>SUISSETEC_MCP_JWKS_URI</info> (the hub's key set) and <info>SUISSETEC_MCP_ISSUER</info> (the hub's base URL).
* Check bundle configuration at <info>packages/suissetec_mcp_auth.yaml</info> - claim schema 3: rights arrive as <comment>entitlements</comment>, mapped with <info>roles.function_mapping</info>.
* Nothing to configure for the hub's <comment>discovery token</comment> - the bundle recognises it and lets it list tools only.
* This bundle brings <comment>no firewall of its own</comment> - add a stateless one in <info>config/packages/security.yaml</info>:

* Guard <info>^/mcp</info> with <comment>IS_AUTHENTICATED_FULLY, not with a role</comment> - the hub's discovery request carries only ROLE_MCP_DISCOVERY, a role there locks the hub out of listing your tools. Put the boundary on each tool (<info>#[IsGranted]</info>).
* The empty provider is needed as soon as the application has more than one provider (Sylius, the portal). Do not replace it with a real one.

* <fg=red>Firewall order matters.</> Symfony uses the FIRST firewall whose pattern matches. In <comment>Sylius</comment> the mcp firewall must sit <comment>ABOVE</comment> the admin and shop firewalls - their regexes (<info>%sylius.security.admin_regex%</info> / <info>%sylius.security.shop_regex%</info>) are broad enough to swallow <info>/mcp</info>, and then the path is never reachable.
* Add the key-set warm-up to your deployment, after the cache clear, so the first request after a release does not pay for the fetch: <info>bin/console suissetec:mcp-auth:warm-jwks</info>

* Inherit the shipped contract test (<info>Suissetec\McpAuthBundle\Test\McpAuthContractTestCase</info>) in <comment>tests/</comment> and feed it this application's own configuration values - it runs the whole token-verification contract against your setup.
* MCP logs are written to <comment>var/log/suissetec_mcp_auth-YYYY-MM.log</comment> (monthly rotation, 3 months retention). Requires <info>symfony/monolog-bundle</info>.
